status_meanings.disputed: sources disagree; both are listed in the record's notes
status_meanings.unverifiable: the fact appears only in secondary sources; no primary source could be obtained
status_meanings.verified: the value in the wiki matches the primary source

records.notes: Absence of branch prediction cannot be proved by a single positive sentence; the correction rests on the datasheet's complete architectural description, which lists the accumulator, index registers, pointer stack, instruction encoding/decoder, timing and control — with no prediction or speculative-fetch mechanism — and defines the fixed cycle in the Instruction Set Format section: a 1-word instruction is 8 bits requiring 8 clock periods (instruction cycle) and a 2-word instruction is 16 bits requiring 16 clock periods (2 instruction cycles). Conditional branching exists (JCN), but it is resolved in the normal instruction cycle, not predicted. records.fact: Retirement mechanics: retirement hardware uses uop timestamps to reimpose program order; when a uop retires the ROB writes its result into the appropriate RRF entry and notifies the RAT; up to 3 uops retire per clock; on a mispredict the machine flushes all or part of its state
records.notes: Level-3 record: the timestamp mechanism and the RRF/RAT commit path; the flush-on-mispredict sentence is 'This retirement process must observe not only the original program order, it must correctly handle interrupts and faults, and flush all or part of its state on detection of a mispredicted branch.'
records.quote: Retirement hardware in the ROB uses uop timestamps to reimpose the original program order on the uops as their results are committed to permanent architectural machine state in the Retirement Register File (RRF). When a uop is retired, the ROB writes that uop's result into the appropriate RRF entry and notifies the RAT of that retirement so that subsequent register renaming can be activated. Up to 3 uops can be retired per clock cycle.

records.current_value: Per PU half: 1 DP or 2 SP FMA; 4/8/16 MACs of 16/8/4-bit data
records.fact: Each PU-half ALU performs one double-precision or two single-precision floating-point multiply-adds, or 4, 8, or 16 multiply-adds of 16-, 8-, or 4-bit data; each ALU result is written to the corresponding accumulator register file while its input can come from either half
records.notes: Companion sentences: 'It can also perform 4, 8, or 16 multiply-adds of 16-, 8-, or 4-bit data, respectively. The result of each ALU is always written to the corresponding accumulator register file but the input can come from either one. (Hence the requirement for two read ports.)'
